R-28 allocation_probe: tracemalloc peak for one isolated candidate evaluation, with the scenario's PROBE_BUILDS build locked into every slot so the optimizer's exact regime scores exactly one option. Three captures of each scenario on the tip; the recorded value is the maximum observed, observed_spread_bytes is the max-minus-min of those three, and the gate margin is Phase 4 S4's 15%. Two consequences a reader must not have to derive. (a) These peaks are LOWER than the mid-phase reading on all four scenarios, so Phase 4 S4's 15% margin is now computed off a smaller number than it would have been at 66072ea -- a tighter absolute ceiling, deliberately, because the smaller number is the true one. (b) observed_spread_bytes is a per-scenario max-minus-min of this tip's three captures, not the campaign's noise band: syndra_mandate_3champ's 126 is twice the 63 the other three show, and it is the one scenario 0A.3 introduced, so the wider band is measured on the newest shape rather than inherited.

pylint holds one row per src/ or scripts/ file Phase 0A touched -- the 18 files 'git diff --name-only 584071e..HEAD -- src/*.py scripts/*.py' names -- each scored by pylint's own json2 scorer through scripts/pylint_ratchet.py --scores. The eight rows 0A.4-0A.10 added are scripts/plan_audit.py, capabilities.py, data_registry.py and the five survival/ modules. Every row here is an enforceable floor, not bookkeeping: 'pylint_ratchet.py --check' fails on any file scoring below its row (R-03). Three of the new rows sit at a perfect 10.0 (scripts/plan_audit.py, capabilities.py, survival/__init__.py), so any lint regression at all in those files is a red gate. Two pre-existing floors were RAISED by this capture rather than merely held -- item_support_effects.py 9.838709677419354 -> 9.839142091152816 and participant_timeline.py 9.698275862068966 -> 9.698795180722891 -- so a later commit landing either file back at its old score now fails a check that was green before, which is the intended direction of a ratchet but is a tightening and is recorded as one.
